criteria.quote: Rhyhorn forgets why it started charging.
criteria.revision: Make the first line create a sharper contradiction: "Rhyhorn can remember only one thing at a time—then it forgets why it started rushing."

criteria.quote: Sometimes, smashing something apparently helps it remember why it started.
If Rhyhorn forgets the goal, what keeps it charging?
criteria.revision: Make the unresolved danger more concrete: "If Rhyhorn forgets why it started—and can barely turn—what finally ends the charge?"

criteria.quote: Short legs cannot turn well, leaving one straight path forward.
criteria.revision: Make the progression move from memory to persistence: replace the second scene's narration with "Once it charges, it won't stop running until it falls asleep," then reveal the forgotten purpose afterward.

criteria.quote: Sometimes, smashing something apparently helps it remember why it started.
Rhyhorn forgets why it started charging.
criteria.revision: Separate the repeated memory beats: use "Once it charges, it won't stop running until it falls asleep" in the opening scene, reserve "It can remember only one thing at a time" for the memory reveal, and keep the demolition detail as the final twist.

criteria.quote: Goal forgotten. Charge intact. Flaw or identity?
criteria.revision: Resolve the opening question with the documented behavior: "The goal disappears, but the charge doesn't. Rhyhorn keeps running until it falls asleep."

criteria.quote: Is forgetting the goal a flaw, or Rhyhorn’s whole identity?
criteria.revision: Make the split turn on the evidence rather than an abstract label: "Is Rhyhorn's charge a failure of memory—or does forgetting the goal make no difference once it starts?"
